    """Example using custom permission prompt tool"""

        #     "command": "npx",
        #     "args": ["-y", "@modelcontextprotocol/server-security"],
        #     "env": {"API_KEY": "your-key"}
        # }
    }

        options=ClaudeCodeOptions(
            permission_prompt_tool_name="mcp__security__approval_prompt",  # Changed from permission_prompt_tool
            mcp_servers=mcp_servers,
            allowed_tools=["Read", "Grep"],
            disallowed_tools=["Bash(rm*)", "Write"],
            system_prompt="You are a security auditor"
        )
    ) as client:

        # Monitor tool usage and permissions
        async for message in client.receive_response():

                    if hasattr(block, 'type'):  # Added check for 'type' attribute
                        if block.type == 'tool_use':
                            print(f"[Tool: {block.name}] ", end='')
                    if hasattr(block, 'text'):
                        print(block.text, end='', flush=True)
            
            # Check for permission denials in error messages
            if type(message).__name__ == "ErrorMessage":
                if hasattr(message, 'error') and "Permission denied" in str(message.error):
                    print(f"\n⚠️ Permission denied: {message.error}")

asyncio.run(use_permission_prompt())

import asyncio

async def use_permission_prompt():
    """Example using custom permission prompt tool"""

        #     "args": ["-y", "@modelcontextprotocol/server-security"],
        #     "env": {"API_KEY": "your-key"}
        # }
    }

            permission_prompt_tool_name="mcp__security__approval_prompt",  # Changed from permission_prompt_tool
            mcp_servers=mcp_servers,
            allowed_tools=["Read", "Grep"],
            disallowed_tools=["Bash(rm*)", "Write"],

                    if hasattr(block, 'text'):
                        print(block.text, end='', flush=True)
            
            # Check for permission denials in error messages
            if type(message).__name__ == "ErrorMessage":
                if hasattr(message, 'error') and "Permission denied" in str(message.error):

TITLE: Implement File Protection Hook
DESCRIPTION: This configuration snippet demonstrates how to set up a 'PreToolUse' hook to intercept 'Edit' or 'MultiEdit' commands. It includes a shell command that checks if the file path contains sensitive patterns like '.env', 'package-lock.json', or '.git/'. If a sensitive file is detected, the hook will exit with a status code of 2, effectively blocking the edit.

SOURCE: https://docs.anthropic.com/en/docs/claude-code/hooks-guide

LANGUAGE: json
CODE:
```
{
  "hooks": {
    "PreToolUse": [
      {
        "matcher": "Edit|MultiEdit|Write",
        "hooks": [
          {
            "type": "command",
            "command": "python3 -c \"import json, sys; data=json.load(sys.stdin); path=data.get('tool_input',{}).get('file_path',''); sys.exit(2 if any(p in path for p in ['.env', 'package-lock.json', '.git/']) else 0)\""
          }
        ]
      }
    ]
  }
}
```

TITLE: Implement File Protection Hook
DESCRIPTION: This configuration snippet demonstrates how to set up a 'PreToolUse' hook to intercept 'Edit' or 'MultiEdit' commands. It includes a shell command that checks if the file path contains sensitive patterns like '.env', 'package-lock.json', or '.git/'. LANGUAGE: json

            "command": "python3 -c \"import json, sys; data=json.load(sys.stdin); path=data.get('tool_input',{}).get('file_path',''); sys.exit(2 if any(p in path for p in ['.env', 'package-lock.json', '.git/']) else 0)\""
          }
        ]
      }
    ]
  }
}
```
